strings: The Wildmane Water Well is the northernmost of the sacred water wells scattered across Mulgore, resting just north of the mesas of Thunder Bluff. Vital to the plains and their herds, it has become a contested flashpoint targeted by goblin opportunists seeking to choke the tauren's lifeblood.

For generations, the nomadic tauren have relied on sacred water wells dug across the golden plains of Mulgore to sustain their people and their wandering kodo herds. The Wildmane Well guards the northern expanse just beyond the shadow of Thunder Bluff. Its vital importance makes it an irresistible target for enemies of the tribes. The goblins of the Venture Company have fouled it with their poisons in a bid to control the regional water supply, and only a cleansing ritual with a totem crafted by the tauren can make its waters pure again.
Where is the Wildmane Water Well located?
The Wildmane Water Well is situated on the plains of Mulgore, directly north of the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff. It is the northernmost of the sacred wells that sustain the region.

Why is the well important to the tauren?
Fresh water is life on the plains. The tauren hold the land's wells sacred as vital lifelines for their settlements, traveling hunters, and the great kodo herds roaming the plains of Mulgore.
why do tauren care about the well | wildmane well sacred

Windbreak Canyon is a winding gorge along the northern side of Thousand Needles, situated between Freewind Post and the Shimmering Flats. Famous for its harsh drafts and jagged stone, it is heavily infested with nesting wind serpents. Travelers passing along the main road must tread carefully near its mouth to avoid being hunted from above.
A Serpent Nest in the Needles

Carved into the sheer northern walls of the canyon floor, Windbreak Canyon spans a large stretch of territory east of Freewind Post. Rather than offering shelter, the ravine channels whistling winds between the rock spires, creating ideal perches for feral wind serpents. The predators lay their clutches along the stone ledges and strike at unwary travelers drifting off the main road. Those braving the canyon interior will also find the winding trails that climb upward toward the Weathered Nook.
Windbreak Canyon lies on the northern side of Thousand Needles, roughly between Freewind Post and the eastern approach to the Shimmering Flats.
windbreak canyon location | where is windbreak canyon | windbreak map

The canyon is dominated by aggressive wild wind serpents that nest among the crags and defend their clutches from intruders.

Following the canyon's rising interior trails leads travelers toward the Weathered Nook nestled in the cliffs above.

Windfury Ridge is a rugged highland area flanking the pastures of Mulgore. Notorious for harboring vicious harpies alongside predatory wolves and cougars, it poses a constant hazard to travelers while offering prized feathers to tauren artisans.

Windfury Ridge rises sharply above Mulgore's serene plains, serving as the hunting grounds of the Windfury harpies. These vicious winged creatures nest high along the crags, readily swooping down upon any unwary wanderers who skirt the hills. The rocky terrain is further populated by prowling prairie wolves and wild mountain cougars, making the ridge one of the more treacherous borders of the tauren heartland. Despite the danger, the harpies are frequently hunted by brave tauren warriors; their vibrant, iridescent plumage is highly sought after across Thunder Bluff to adorn ceremonial garments for lavish feasts and wedding celebrations.

The ridge is teeming with predatory cougars and prairie wolves, but its most persistent menace is the flock of aggressive harpies nesting along the heights. They actively dive from the crags to capture or butcher intruders who wander too close to their nesting sites.
why is windfury ridge dangerous | hazards of windfury ridge | windfury ridge monsters
Why do the tauren hunt the harpies on Windfury Ridge?

Beyond securing the borders from their predations, tauren hunt the Windfury harpies for their brilliant feathers. These colorful plumes are traditionally harvested and woven into ceremonial headdresses and decorations used during feasts and weddings.
why kill windfury harpies | harpy feathers mulgore | hunting harpies
Windfury Ridge lies along the elevated bluffs in the pastoral region of Mulgore, in the far north of Mulgore, beyond Thunder Bluff.

The ridge is both a recurring nuisance to young hunters and a source of vital ceremonial ornaments used to honor marriages and seasonal gatherings.

Windshear Crag is a heavily despoiled valley in the central Stonetalon Mountains, stripped of its ancient timber by the Venture Company. Once a lush forest, the region is now an industrial wasteland dominated by whirring shredders, murky runoff, and aggressive logging crews. In the shadows of the machinery, local kobolds burrow for ore while mountain passes connect the scarred landscape to Ashenvale.

Not long ago, Windshear Crag was a thick, old-growth woodland flanking the slopes of Stonetalon. That tranquil wilderness vanished when the Venture Company arrived in search of profit. Today, the basin is filled with severed stumps, acrid smog, and clanking machinery. The entire logging enterprise is overseen by Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a leper gnome whose engineering genius produced the Super Reaper 6000—a mechanical terror capable of reducing massive trunks to kindling in moments. From an elevated platform above the polluted Cragpool Lake, Gerenzo directs an unchecked operation that strips the mountain bare, earning the hostility of rival engineers and local inhabitants alike.

Beyond the active timberyards, Windshear Crag holds other hazards and crossroads. To the southeast lies Windshear Mine, where territorial kobolds dig through the rock for Smoky Iron Ingots, fiercely attacking anyone who nears their haul. In the crag's northeast reaches, travelers can find the Talondeep Path, an underground cavern tunnel threading straight beneath the ridges into Ashenvale. Stationed near this shadowed portal stands the tauren elder Braug Dimspirit, who tests the historical wisdom and resolve of Horde wayfarers venturing through the contested peaks.
Who is running the logging operation here?

The logging venture is commanded on-site by Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a brilliant but contaminated leper gnome engineer. Operating under contract with the Venture Company, he watches over the crag from a timber platform raised directly over Cragpool Lake.
who leads venture co here | who is the boss of windshear | gerenzo wrenchwhistle lore

The Super Reaper 6000 is an advanced mechanical logging prototype engineered by Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. Designed to clear timber at unprecedented speeds, it can grind ancient mountain trees into sawdust within moments, accelerating the company's clear-cutting.

Winterfall Village is a sprawling furbolg encampment nestled in the snowdrifts of eastern Winterspring, just east of Everlook. Once peaceful kin to the other ursine tribes of Kalimdor, the Winterfall furbolgs living here have descended into madness and violent corruption under the rule of High Chief Winterfall.

Sprawled across the terraced snowbanks east of the goblin trading post Everlook, Winterfall Village serves as the primary bastion of the Winterfall furbolgs in Winterspring. Like their cousins scattered across northern Kalimdor, these bear-folk were warped and driven mad by the lingering foulness of the Burning Legion's invasion. Led by High Chief Winterfall from a secluded cavern atop the settlement's highest tier, the tribe has abandoned its ancestral ways. Instead of communing peacefully with the wild spirits of the snow, the enraged furbolgs now aggressively assault travelers, patrol the mountain passes, and threaten any who come near their frost-bitten home.
It is the central settlement of the Winterfall furbolgs, located on the snowy slopes just east of the goblin outpost Everlook in Winterspring.
winterfall village info | what is this place | furbolg town winterspring

The Winterfall furbolgs succumbed to corruption following the Third War. The demonic taint left behind by the Burning Legion warped their minds, stripping away their peaceful customs and leaving them violently hostile to all outsiders.

The fall of the Winterfall tribe marks another painful fracture in the ancient bonds between the night elves and the native peoples of Kalimdor.

The Winterhoof Water Well is a vital fresh water source situated on the edge of the Rolling Plains in southern Mulgore. Crucial to the local wildlife and nomadic tauren tribes, the well has recently fallen under threat from the exploitative Venture Company, who seek to poison and control the region's water supply.

In the arid stretches of central Kalimdor, water is life, and Mulgore's subterranean wells sustain both the herds of the plains and the encampments of the tauren. The Winterhoof Water Well, named for one of the respected tribes of the plains, taps into the deep aquifers beneath the Rolling Plains. Unfortunately, its strategic importance has drawn the avarice of the Venture Company. Rather than sharing the land or negotiating, the ruthless goblin cartel has attempted to poison the water supply to exert leverage over the surrounding territory.

To counter the industrial sabotage of the Venture Company, tauren elders and shamans have mobilized young braves across Mulgore. Mull Thunderhorn has crafted sacred totems designed to counter the industrial toxins and restore the spiritual and physical balance of the well. Cleansing the well is not merely an act of survival for the tauren, but a spiritual duty to ensure that the earth and its waters remain uncorrupted by foreign greed.
Where is the Winterhoof Water Well located?
The well is located in southern Mulgore, right on the fringes of the Rolling Plains south of Bloodhoof Village.
winterhoof well location | where is winterhoof well | find winterhoof water well

Beyond providing necessary hydration for tribes and roaming herds, water sources in Mulgore are viewed as gifts from the Earth Mother. Corrupting them is considered both a direct physical threat and a severe spiritual affront.

Witch Hill is a dreary, mist-shrouded rise in the heart of Dustwallow Marsh along the path toward Theramore. It is best known for the secluded Swamplight Manor, scattered camps of hostile Mirefin murlocs, and sinister rumors of dark hauntings.

Rising out of the stagnant waters of Dustwallow Marsh, Witch Hill sits roughly a third of the way along the peninsula leading southeast toward Theramore Isle. The elevated ground provides little refuge from the hazards of the swamp, as aggressive Mirefin murlocs claim the surrounding waters. At its center stands Swamplight Manor, the lonely and unsettling residence of the hermit known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl. Travelers passing through frequently report eerie phenomena and lingering dark presences across the knoll.

Behind its quiet, gloomy exterior, Witch Hill is steeped in dark rumor. Tales of hauntings cling to the desolate ground, adding to the local paranoia. Those who brave the hill must contend not only with the primitive savagery of the Mirefin, but with occult threats that make even seasoned Theramore patrols uneasy.
Witch Hill is located in Dustwallow Marsh, situated about a third of the way down the peninsula that connects the western marsh to Theramore Isle.

Witherbark Village is a forest troll settlement nestled around a secluded lake in the southeastern hills of the Arathi Highlands. Inhabited by the hostile Witherbark tribe, it serves as a staging ground for troll raiders contesting both the Alliance remnants of Stromgarde and the Horde outpost at Hammerfall.

Built along the shores of a quiet mountain lake, Witherbark Village houses the fierce forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe. While fishers, axe throwers, and witch doctors occupy the hut-lined waterfront, tribal leaders such as Zalas Witherbark and deadly shadow hunters oversee operations from a massive cavern cavern tucked behind the settlement. The Witherbark maintain an opportunistic alliance with the Boulderfist ogres of Arathi, working together to carve out territory across the highlands—even establishing a firm foothold amidst the ruins of Stromgarde Keep. Fiercely territorial, they lash out at any outsider venturing into their corner of the basin.

The settlement is held by the Witherbark tribe, a faction of forest trolls indigenous to the region. They field headhunters, axe throwers, fishers, and witch doctors who defend the lake and surrounding paths.

Woodpaw Den is a rugged gnoll stronghold nestled in northern Feralas, just north of the ancient Darkmist Ruins. The settlement serves as a major gathering point for the Woodpaw gnolls and their fiercest pack alphas, making it a dangerous pocket of wilderness within the dense canopy.

Situated amidst the towering boughs of Feralas, Woodpaw Den stands as the fortified heartland of the local Woodpaw gnolls. Unlike smaller scout camps scattered along the jungle tracks, this encampment is heavily guarded by the pack's seasoned Alphas. The gnolls here defend their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and the encroaching wilderness. Located just north of the elven remnants at Darkmist Ruins, the den represents an ever-present predatory threat to travelers attempting to traverse the central wilderness of the region.
Woodpaw Den is a prominent settlement and encampment of the Woodpaw gnolls in northern Feralas, situated just north of the Darkmist Ruins. It is heavily inhabited by the pack's dangerous Alphas.

The Woodpaw Hills are a rugged, forested stretch of southeastern Feralas claimed by the Woodpaw gnolls. Once a dominant tribal territory, the hills have become an embattled frontline as insectoid terrors tunnel up from below and ancient stone giants stalk the canopy.

The dense forests of the Woodpaw Hills serve as the historical territory of the Woodpaw gnoll clan. While the hyena-folk once roamed unchallenged across these slopes, their dominance has crumbled under pressure from multiple fronts. To their southeast, nightmarish silithid swarmers have breached the earth at the Writhing Deep, forcing the gnolls back and compelling their chieftains to retreat deeper into the Woodpaw Den. Adding to the peril, ancient mountain giants—relics summoned down during the Third War to repel the Burning Legion—now wander the hillside woods, crushing any travelers or Horde interlopers who stray into their path.
Who lives in the Woodpaw Hills?

The hills are primarily occupied by the Woodpaw clan of gnolls, who maintain defensive camps throughout the woods. Ancient mountain giants also patrol the slopes, while invasive silithid insects push in from the southeastern borders.

The Workshop Entrance, commonly known as the backdoor to Gnomeregan, is an access portal situated just beyond the Train Depot. It provides seasoned adventurers and engineers an alternative route into the depths of the irradiated city, bypassing the front gates and opening near the Engineering Labs.

Located across the cavernous workshop floor just past the Train Depot, the Workshop Entrance offers a direct approach into the industrial heart of Gnomeregan. Flanked on one side by the opening to the Loading Room, this passage cuts straight through to the Engineering Labs, avoiding the fortified entry gates that leper gnomes and troggs contest near the surface. For strike teams attempting to reclaim the underground capital, bypassing the initial perimeter through this side door can prove vital.

The Workshop Entrance sits on the far side of the workshop floor, past the Train Depot in the outer corridors of Gnomeregan. From this vantage, the portal to the Loading Room lies to your left.

The Writhing Deep is a massive, insectoid hive complex carved into southeastern Feralas. Inhabited by the Zukk'ash silithid, this subterranean burrow is a growing danger that threatens nearby wildlife and surrounding encampments alike. The relentless expansion of these subterranean predators has upset the regional balance of the lush forest.

Tucked away in the humid lowlands of southeastern Feralas, the Writhing Deep serves as the primary colony for the Zukk'ash silithid. Unlike the typical woodland beasts of the valley, these chittering insects dig labyrinthine tunnels and fiercely guard clutches of resinous eggs. The hive's aggressive encroachment into the nearby territories has destabilized the wild fauna and agitated local gnoll packs, pushing displaced and frenzied predators uncomfortably close to both Horde paths and native sanctuaries.

The chasm is infested by the Zukk'ash silithid, an aggressive breed of giant insects comprising workers, tunnelers, stingers, and wasps led by dangerous brood champions such as Stinglasher and Qirot.

The Writhing Haunt is a blighted farmstead situated east of the Ruins of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands. Once fertile land that fed Lordaeron, it has been seized by the Scourge and transformed into a toxic spreading ground for plague vapors.

Like many of the old human homesteads surrounding Andorhal, the farmstead now called the Writhing Haunt fell swiftly during the Third War. Today, the fields do not grow crops but instead harvest rot. The Scourge planted an enormous plague cauldron squarely in the center of the tilled earth, continuously venting noxious, diseased vapors into the air. Rotting ghouls, freezing ghouls, and fetid zombies wander the overgrown furrows, guarding the machinery under the command of Cauldron Lord Razarch.

Despite the omnipresent danger of the Scourge and the choking miasma from the cauldron, the farm is not entirely abandoned by the living. Tucked away inside one of the dilapidated farmhouses hides Mulgris Deepriver. Seeking a way to neutralize the spreading contagion and strike back against the plague apparatus, he observes the cauldron's operation and awaits capable travelers willing to confront Razarch and disrupt the Scourge's foul enterprise.
What was the Writhing Haunt before the plague?
Before the Third War, the Writhing Haunt was a productive, life-sustaining human farm that helped supply grain and livestock to nearby Andorhal and the greater Kingdom of Lordaeron.

Wyrmbog is the perilous southern expanse of Dustwallow Marsh, lying just south of the Dragonmurk. Dominated by foul mire and jagged spires of stone, it serves as the staging ground and territorial buffer for the black dragonflight. The caves of ancient wyrms, including the broodmother Onyxia and the elder Emberstrife, are carved directly into its surrounding ridges.

Wyrmbog represents the most heavily infested black dragon territory in southern Kalimdor. Where the open waters of Dustwallow give way to scorched muck and towering bones, whelps and mature drakes patrol the fetid air. The bog is choked with toxic fumes and predatory beasts driven wild by the draconic presence. Travelers foolish enough to wander into these reaches find themselves directly in the shadow of Onyxia's Lair and Emberstrife's cavernous den.
Wyrmbog is the treacherous southern region of Dustwallow Marsh, situated south of the Dragonmurk. It is heavily infested with members of the black dragonflight.
